bug_semantics: deepExtend() enumerated attacker-controlled own keys and used Reflect.has() on the merge receiver. For a JSON-parsed __proto__ key, Reflect.has({}, '__proto__') is true through Object.prototype's inherited accessor; because both resolved values are objects, the recursive branch calls extendObject(Object.prototype, attackerValue), and the attacker's nested keys are then assigned onto Object.prototype. Every subsequently created ordinary object inherits the injected properties, enabling application-dependent integrity, availability, or authorization failures wherever untrusted data reaches deepExtend().
flaw_origin: Commit ece027428a9a5755916f159a5760665be9cc89a6 changed the receiver test from !o1.hasOwnProperty(key) to !Reflect.has(o1, key) while retaining recursive merging and no forbidden-key filter. That semantic change made inherited __proto__ look like an existing object-valued destination and redirected recursion into Object.prototype. Earlier code could alter the returned object's own prototype via __proto__ assignment, but the advisory's realm-wide Object.prototype write primitive was absent until this commit.
